label: History
value: James A. is the subject of the wiki page
unit: Mr. James A. Harrison moves to Avonlea and buys the farm neighboring Green Gables. His first encounter with Anne Shirley is contentious when her jersey cow, Dolly, breaks into his wheat field, leading to a fiery exchange of insults. However, the two quickly overcome their bad start and become close friends, often sharing tea and conversations. He confides in Anne about his parrot, Ginger, whose profane language causes Mr. Harrison much embarrassment. When Ginger unexpectedly dies, Mr. Harrison buries him quietly, though he secretly misses the bird. Later, his estranged wife, Emily Harrison, unexpectedly arrives in Avonlea, revealing that Mr. Harrison was married all along. Through Anne's peacemaking and Emily's domestic influence, the couple resolves their past differences and reunites, turning their household into a neat and happy home.

label: History
value: Gilbert's resignation initiates a close friendship between him and Anne.
unit: Gilbert first meets Anne Shirley at Avonlea School, where he famously pulls her red hair and calls her 'Carrots,' earning a slate smashed over his head and years of cold resentment from her. Despite Anne's grudge, Gilbert consistently attempts to apologize and protect her, competing with her academically throughout their school years and at Queen's Academy. Upon graduation from Queen's, he selflessly resigns his position as Avonlea's schoolteacher so Anne can stay at Green Gables after Matthew Cuthbert's death, which finally breaks the ice between them and initiates a close friendship. He later attends Redmond College alongside Anne, where he excels academically and in student life while continuing to harbor romantic feelings for her. During their junior year, Gilbert proposes to Anne, but she rejects him, claiming she only cares for him as a friend, which causes a painful distance between them. After graduating from Redmond, Gilbert contracts a life-threatening case of typhoid fever, which causes Anne to realize her true feelings for him. Upon his recovery, Gilbert learns of her changed heart and proposes to her a second time at Hester Gray's garden, where she happily accepts him.

label: History

unit: Mr. Phillips serves as the schoolmaster at Avonlea when Anne Shirley first attends school. On Anne's first day, he severely humbles and embarrasses her by misspelling her name on the blackboard and forcing her to sit next to Gilbert Blythe as punishment for being late. His harsh and public punishments lead Anne to refuse to attend school for several months. Throughout his tenure, he openly woos one of his oldest students, Prissy Andrews, paying far more attention to her than to his instructional duties. At the end of his school term, he leaves Avonlea, much to the relief of most of his students.

label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables
unit: Matthew Cuthbert lives at Green Gables in Avonlea with his unmarried sister, Marilla. Deciding they need help with farm chores as Matthew grows older, they arrange to adopt an orphan boy from Nova Scotia. When Matthew goes to the Bright River train station to fetch the child, he finds eleven-year-old Anne Shirley instead, as a mistake had been made. Despite his paralyzing shyness, Matthew is immediately charmed by Anne's imaginative talk during the ride home and quietly insists to Marilla that they keep her. Over the next several years, Matthew acts as Anne's devoted confidant, secretly spoiling her with treats like a dress with puffed sleeves. When Anne earns a scholarship to Queen's Academy and later passes her exams with distinction, Matthew takes immense pride in her achievements. Shortly after Anne returns home for the summer, Matthew suffers a fatal heart attack upon reading that the Abbey Bank, where his life savings were deposited, has failed. His love and belief in Anne leave a lasting impact on her life, prompting her to stay at Green Gables to care for Marilla.
